title: Bounded quantified formula calls
statement: Let $x$ and $qs$ be Boolean words, let $B$ be a natural number, and let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula over natural-number variables. Suppose $x$ is the pair encoding of $qs$ and the serialization of $\varphi$, that $2^{|qs|+1}\le B$, and that $|x|\le B$. For every pair of natural numbers $j,k$ with $k+j=|qs|$, and every $S<2^{k+1}$, the machine reaches, from the node state with depth $k$, assignment stack $S$, and input pointer $0$, the return state carrying the truth value of evaluating $\varphi$ under the remaining quantifiers of $qs$ and the assignment encoded by $(k,S)$; the ending depth, stack, and input pointer are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $x$ is the pair encoding of $qs$ and the serialization of $\varphi$
replaced:
Let $x$ be a bit string, $B$ a natural number, $qs$ a bit string of quantifiers, and
$\varphi$ a CNF formula. Suppose $x=\langle
qs,\operatorname{serialize}(\varphi)\rangle$, $2^{|qs|+1}\le B$, and $|x|\le B$. Then
for every pair of natural numbers $j,k$ with $k+j=|qs|$, and every stack value
$S<2^{k+1}$, the machine starting at a node with depth $k$, stack $S$, and input pointer
$0$ reaches the return state whose answer is the truth value of the quantified-formula
evaluation of $\varphi$ on the remaining quantifiers of $qs$ under the assignment
encoded by $(k,S)$, with the same depth, stack, and pointer. Every configuration before
the end of this run satisfies the machine's validity conditions and has all registers at
most $B$.
